title.en: Volume 354 Biographies 141: Wan Chengfeng, Zhou Xiying, Qian Yue, Qin Ying, Li Zonghan, Han Dingjin, Zhu Fangzeng
title.raw: 卷354 列傳一百四十一 万承风 周系英 钱樾 秦瀛 李宗瀚 韩鼎晋 朱方增

sentences.zh: 列傳一百四十一

translations.literal: Biographies 141
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 141

sentences.zh: 萬承風周系英錢樾秦瀛李宗瀚韓鼎晉朱方增

translations.literal: Wan Chengfeng, Zhou Xiying, Qian Yue, Qin Ying, Li Zonghan, Han Dingjin, and Zhu Fangzeng
translations.idiomatic: Wan Chengfeng, Zhou Xiying, Qian Yue, Qin Ying, Li Zonghan, Han Dingjin, and Zhu Fangzeng

sentences.zh: 萬承風，字和圃，江西義寧人。

translations.literal: Wan Chengfeng, styled Hepu, was a native of Yining in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Chengfeng, whose style was Hepu, came from Yining in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十六年進士，選庶吉士，授檢討。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year of the Qianlong reign he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the forty-sixth year of Qianlong, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was made a reviser.

sentences.zh: 直上書房，侍宣宗讀。

translations.literal: He served in the Upper Study and attended the future Xuanzong in his studies.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted to the Upper Study, where he tutored the future Emperor Xuanzong.

sentences.zh: 六十年，典試雲南。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year he served as chief examiner for Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixtieth year of Qianlong he presided over the provincial examination in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 時仁宗在潛邸，賜詩寵行。

translations.literal: At that time the future Renzong was still in his princely residence and bestowed a poem to honor his departure.
translations.idiomatic: The future Emperor Renzong, still heir apparent, honored his departure with an imperial poem.

sentences.zh: 累遷翰林院侍讀。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to reader-in-waiting in the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to reader-in-waiting in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶三年，大考，降檢討。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiaqing, at the great triennial evaluation, he was demoted to reviser.
translations.idiomatic: At the triennial evaluation in the third year of Jiaqing he was demoted back to reviser.

sentences.zh: 四年，督廣東學政。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed provincial education commissioner for Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made education commissioner of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 瓊州海寇猝發，承風以聞，命總督吉慶按治，總兵西密揚阿等以恇怯置吏議。

translations.literal: Pirates suddenly rose at Qiongzhou; Chengfeng reported it, and the court ordered Governor-General Ji Qing to investigate, while Regional Commander Ximiyang'a and others were referred for official discipline on charges of cowardice.
translations.idiomatic: When pirates suddenly struck Qiongzhou, Chengfeng reported the crisis; the court ordered Governor-General Ji Qing to investigate, and Regional Commander Ximiyang'a and others were brought up for discipline on charges of cowardice.

sentences.zh: 累遷侍講學士，任滿還京，直上書房，擢詹事。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to expositor of the Hanlin Academy; when his term ended he returned to the capital, re-entered the Upper Study, and was promoted to grand tutor of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to expositor of the Hanlin Academy, and when his term ended he returned to the capital, resumed service in the Upper Study, and was appointed grand tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 督山東學政，整厲士習，扶持善類。

translations.literal: As education commissioner of Shandong he tightened scholarly conduct and supported the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: As education commissioner of Shandong he tightened scholarly standards and championed men of integrity.

sentences.zh: 洊擢禮部侍郎，命還京。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to vice minister of rites and ordered back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in due course to vice minister of rites and recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 十二年，督學江蘇。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he supervised education in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was appointed education commissioner of Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 以清江浦、荷花塘河工取勢太直，屢築屢圮，奏請復舊，詔如議行。

translations.literal: Because the river works at Qingjiangpu and Hehuatang took too straight a course and were repeatedly built and repeatedly collapsed, he memorialized to restore the old alignment, and an edict approved his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Finding that the Qingjiangpu and Hehuatang works ran too straight and had been rebuilt only to collapse again, he memorialized to restore the former course; the throne approved and ordered it carried out.

sentences.zh: 調兵部。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 十四年，上五旬萬壽，陳請解任還京祝嘏，詔嚴斥，左遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, at the emperor's fiftieth-birthday celebration, he asked to resign his post and return to the capital to offer congratulations; an edict sternly rebuked him and he was demoted to grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, when the emperor celebrated his fiftieth birthday, Chengfeng asked to leave his post and return to the capital to offer congratulations; the throne rebuked him sharply and demoted him to grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 調安徽學政。

translations.literal: He was transferred as education commissioner of Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as education commissioner of Anhui.

sentences.zh: 定遠士子與鳳陽胥役有隙，至試期輒修怨，當事者庇胥役，士益憤，承風疏請下巡撫嚴治胥役，置諸法。

translations.literal: Scholars of Dingyuan had a feud with runners from Fengyang; at each examination season old grievances were renewed, and those in authority shielded the runners, so the scholars grew angrier. Chengfeng memorialized asking the governor to punish the runners severely and bring them to justice.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars in Dingyuan were at odds with clerical runners from Fengyang, and each examination season revived their quarrel while local officials shielded the runners, deepening the scholars' anger. Chengfeng memorialized the governor to punish the runners severely and bring them to justice.

sentences.zh: 擢兵部侍郎，還京，仍直上書房，充經筵講官。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice minister of war, returned to the capital, again served in the Upper Study, and was appointed lecturer at the Classics Colloquium.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to vice minister of war, he returned to the capital, resumed service in the Upper Study, and became a lecturer at the Classics Colloquium.

sentences.zh: 十七年，引疾歸，尋卒，入祀鄉賢祠。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he retired on grounds of illness, soon died, and was enshrined in the local worthies' temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he retired citing illness, died soon after, and was enshrined in his district's temple of local worthies.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，追念舊學，贈禮部尚書銜，諡文恪。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong ascended the throne he recalled their old studies together and posthumously granted the rank of minister of rites with the posthumous title Wenge.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong took the throne he remembered their years as tutor and pupil and posthumously granted him minister of rites with the posthumous title Wenge.

sentences.zh: 道光十二年，晉贈太傅，子方楙等加恩有差。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Daoguang he was further posthumously made grand tutor, and his sons Fangmao and others received differentiated favors.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Daoguang he was further posthumously honored as grand tutor, and his sons Fangmao and others received differentiated imperial favors.

sentences.zh: 周系英，字孟才，湖南湘潭人。

translations.literal: Zhou Xiying, styled Mengcai, was a native of Xiangtan in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xiying, whose style was Mengcai, came from Xiangtan in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五十八年進士，選庶吉士，授編修，累遷侍講。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifty-eighth year of Qianlong, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, appointed compiler, and promoted in succession to expositor.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the fifty-eighth year of Qianlong, entered the Hanlin Academy, was made a compiler, and rose to expositor.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十年，督四川學政。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Jiaqing he was appointed provincial education commissioner for Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Jiaqing he became education commissioner of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 十四年，入直南書房，擢太常寺卿。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he entered regular duty in the Southern Study and was promoted to director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he entered regular duty in the Southern Study and was promoted to director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 尋改直上書房，授三阿哥讀。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was transferred to the Upper Study to instruct the Third Imperial Son.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to the Upper Study to tutor the Third Imperial Son.

sentences.zh: 上諭：「不但授讀講習詩文，當教阿哥為人居心以忠厚為本。」

translations.literal: The emperor instructed: "You must not only teach reading and lecture on poetry and prose; you should teach the prince that in conduct of life sincerity and loyalty are the foundation."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor instructed him: "You must teach the prince more than poetry and prose — you must ground his character in sincerity and loyalty."

sentences.zh: 系英請加授資治通鑑，以知古今治亂興衰之故，悉民間疾苦，上韙之。

translations.literal: Xiying asked to add instruction in the Comprehensive Mirror for Aid in Government so that the prince might know the causes of rise and fall through the ages and understand the people's hardships; the emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: Xiying asked to add the Comprehensive Mirror so the prince would understand how dynasties rise and fall and know the people's hardships; the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 轉光祿寺卿，督山西學政。

translations.literal: He was transferred to director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and appointed education commissioner of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He became director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and education commissioner of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 任滿回京，仍直上書房。

translations.literal: When his term ended he returned to the capital and again served in the Upper Study.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he returned to the capital and resumed service in the Upper Study.

sentences.zh: 十九年，擢兵部右侍郎，母憂去，服闋，補吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was promoted to vice minister of the right in the Ministry of War; he left office on his mother's death, and after mourning was appointed vice minister of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he was made vice minister of war on the right; he left office to mourn his mother, and after the mourning period was appointed vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，湘潭民與江西客民閧，相殺傷，巡撫吳邦慶亦籍江西，陳奏偏袒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year natives of Xiangtan and migrant settlers from Jiangxi clashed and killed and wounded one another; Governor Wu Bangqing, who was also a native of Jiangxi, memorialized in partial favor of his fellow provincials.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year locals in Xiangtan clashed with migrant settlers from Jiangxi, leaving casualties; Governor Wu Bangqing, himself a Jiangxi native, memorialized in a way that favored his fellow provincials.

sentences.zh: 系英詢齎奏人，得事始末，於召對時面陳，乃調邦慶福建，詔以獄事畀總督察治。

translations.literal: Xiying questioned the memorial bearer and learned how the affair began and ended; at an imperial audience he stated it in person, whereupon Bangqing was transferred to Fujian and an edict assigned the case to the governor-general for investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Xiying questioned the memorial bearer and learned the full story; at an imperial audience he laid it out in person, and Bangqing was transferred to Fujian while the case was assigned to the governor-general for investigation.

sentences.zh: 系英素以樸直被眷遇，邦慶初與善，約地方事有見聞必告，至是手書言其曲直；

translations.literal: Xiying had long been favored for his plain integrity; Bangqing had been on good terms with him at first and agreed that whatever he learned of local affairs he would report, and now wrote in his own hand about right and wrong in the case;
translations.idiomatic: Xiying had long been favored for his plain integrity; Bangqing had been friendly with him and had agreed to keep him informed of local affairs, and now wrote in his own hand about the rights and wrongs of the case;

sentences.zh: 系英子汝楨亦致書在籍給事中石承藻詢獄事：書並為邦慶得，先後以兩書上聞。

translations.literal: Xiying's son Ruzhen also wrote to the retired supervising secretary Shi Chengzao to inquire about the case; both letters fell into Bangqing's hands and were reported to the throne in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Xiying's son Ruzhen also wrote the retired supervising secretary Shi Chengzao to inquire about the case; Bangqing obtained both letters and reported them to the throne in succession.

sentences.zh: 上怒系英庇鄉人，部議革職，猶命以編修用。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry that Xiying had shielded his fellow townspeople; the ministry recommended dismissal from office, yet he was still ordered employed as a compiler.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry that Xiying had shielded his fellow townspeople; the ministry recommended dismissal, yet he was still allowed to serve as a compiler.

sentences.zh: 繼以汝楨致書事，褫職回籍。

translations.literal: Subsequently, because of Ruzhen's letter, he was stripped of office and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruzhen's letter came to light, he was stripped of office and sent home.

sentences.zh: 道光初，以四品京堂召用，歷翰林院侍讀學士、內閣學士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daoguang he was recalled as a fourth-rank capital official and served in succession as reader of the Hanlin Academy and grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Daoguang reign he was recalled as a fourth-rank capital official and rose through reader of the Hanlin Academy to grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二年，遷工部侍郎，督江西學政，尋調江蘇，許密摺言地方利病，人才臧否。

translations.literal: In the second year he was transferred to vice minister of works, appointed education commissioner of Jiangxi, soon transferred to Jiangsu, and permitted to submit secret memorials on local advantages and ills and on the worth of men.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he became vice minister of works and education commissioner of Jiangxi, soon transferred to Jiangsu with permission to submit secret memorials on local conditions and the merit of officials.

sentences.zh: 會瀕江大水，學政駐江陰，系英目擊災狀，貽書督撫，留官吏素得民者治賑務，假庫帑三萬兩購米平糶，民感之。

translations.literal: When great floods struck along the river, the education commissioner was stationed at Jiangyin; Xiying witnessed the disaster, wrote to the governor and provincial commander, kept officials who had long won the people's trust to manage relief, borrowed thirty thousand taels from the treasury to buy grain and sell it at fair price, and the people were grateful.
translations.idiomatic: When catastrophic floods struck the river districts he was stationed at Jiangyin; witnessing the disaster, he wrote the governor-general and governor to retain trusted officials for relief work, borrowed thirty thousand taels from the treasury to buy grain and sell it at fair price, and won the people's gratitude.

sentences.zh: 四年，調戶部左侍郎，卒於任。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to vice minister of the left in the Ministry of Revenue and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was made vice minister of revenue on the left and died in office.

sentences.zh: 錢樾，字黼棠，浙江嘉善人。

translations.literal: Qian Yue, styled Futang, was a native of Jiashan in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Yue, whose style was Futang, came from Jiashan in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十七年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the thirty-seventh year of Qianlong, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the thirty-seventh year of Qianlong, entered the Hanlin Academy, and was made a compiler.

sentences.zh: 典陝西鄉試，督四川學政。

translations.literal: He presided over the Shaanxi provincial examination and was appointed education commissioner of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He presided over the Shaanxi provincial examination and served as education commissioner of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 直上書房。

translations.literal: He served in the Upper Study.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the Upper Study.

sentences.zh: 兩典江西鄉試，督廣西學政，累擢少詹事。

translations.literal: He twice presided over the Jiangxi provincial examination, was education commissioner of Guangxi, and was promoted in succession to junior grand tutor of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He twice presided over the Jiangxi provincial examination, served as education commissioner of Guangxi, and rose to junior grand tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年，還京，仍入直。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaqing he returned to the capital and again entered regular palace duty.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jiaqing he returned to the capital and resumed regular palace duty.

sentences.zh: 驟遷內閣學士、禮部侍郎，督江蘇學政。

translations.literal: He was suddenly promoted to grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat and vice minister of rites, and appointed education commissioner of Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: He was rapidly promoted to grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat and vice minister of rites, and made education commissioner of Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 時吳縣令甄輔廷治諸生糾控罪過當，學政平恕曲徇所請，斥革生員二十五人。

translations.literal: At that time the magistrate of Wu county, Zhen Futing, had handled student complaints with excessive penalties; Education Commissioner Pingshu bent the rules to grant his requests and expelled twenty-five licentiates.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate of Wu county, Zhen Futing, had punished student complaints too harshly; Education Commissioner Pingshu indulged his requests and expelled twenty-five licentiates.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，解平恕任，以樾代，至則先复諸生名，僅坐首事者三人，士民稱慶。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it he removed Pingshu from office and replaced him with Yue; on arrival Yue first restored the students' status and punished only three ringleaders, and scholars and common people rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor learned of this he removed Pingshu and sent Yue in his place; on arrival Yue first restored the students' standing and punished only three ringleaders, to the joy of scholars and townspeople alike.

sentences.zh: 方其赴任，途中見行船有大書「內廷南府」者，因上疏劾姦吏詭託，上累聖明，詔飭關津禁絕，嚴罪所司。

translations.literal: On his way to his post he saw traveling boats boldly marked "Inner Court Southern Residence"; he therefore memorialized impeaching corrupt clerks for fraudulent pretense that reflected on the emperor's sagacity, and an edict ordered passes and fords forbidden and the responsible officials severely punished.
translations.idiomatic: On his way to his post he saw boats boldly marked "Inner Court Southern Residence"; he memorialized against corrupt clerks whose fraud reflected on the throne, and an edict closed the passes and severely punished those responsible.

sentences.zh: 時南河邵壩決口，瓜、儀私梟充斥，為閭閻害，命樾密訪以聞。

translations.literal: At that time the Shao dam on the Southern Canal had burst; smugglers filled Guazhou and Yizhen and harmed the common people, and Yue was ordered to investigate secretly and report.
translations.idiomatic: The Shao dam on the Southern Canal had burst, smugglers infested Guazhou and Yizhen and preyed on the people, and Yue was ordered to investigate in secret and report.

sentences.zh: 疏陳：「黃河自豫東界至桃、宿以上，水緩沙停，致河高堤淺，所在防潰。

translations.literal: In his memorial he stated: "From the eastern border of Henan up to Taoyuan and Suzhou, the Yellow River's current slows and sand settles, so the riverbed rises and the dikes grow shallow, and breaches are feared everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: In his memorial he wrote: "From eastern Henan upstream to Taoyuan and Suzhou, the Yellow River runs slow and drops its silt, raising the riverbed and shallowing the dikes, so breaches are feared everywhere.

sentences.zh: 請於霜降後鳩工疏正河，並增築堤防，先務所急。

translations.literal: He asked that after Frost's Descent labor be gathered to dredge and straighten the river and strengthen the dikes, tackling first what was most urgent.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that after Frost's Descent workers be mobilized to dredge the channel and strengthen the dikes, beginning with the most urgent stretches.

sentences.zh: 又以私梟為患，皆由官鹽價貴，民利食私，若稍平鹽價，則私梟自絕。」

translations.literal: He also said that smuggling was a scourge because official salt was costly and the people profited by eating contraband salt; if the salt price were slightly lowered, smugglers would disappear of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that smuggling thrived because official salt was overpriced and the people preferred contraband; moderate the price, he said, and smuggling would die out on its own."

sentences.zh: 疏入，俱報可。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, all proposals were approved.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved every proposal in the memorial.

sentences.zh: 尋調吏部，任滿回京，調戶部，兼管錢法堂事務。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel; when his term ended he returned to the capital, was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue, and concurrently managed affairs of the Bureau of Currency.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, and when his term ended he returned to the capital, moved to the Ministry of Revenue, and concurrently managed the Bureau of Currency.

sentences.zh: 奏請申禁改漕折色，以清弊端。

translations.literal: He memorialized to reiterate the ban on converting grain transport payments to cash, in order to clear away abuses.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to enforce the ban on converting grain-transport quotas to cash payments, so as to curb corruption.

sentences.zh: 復調吏部，九年，坐失察書吏舞弊，以告病治中趙曰濂虛選運同，降內閣學士，樾上疏置辯，議革職，加恩賜編修。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to the Ministry of Personnel; in the ninth year, for failure to detect clerical fraud in which the acting director of the Bureau of Transmission Zhao Yuelian had falsely selected a transport intendant while reporting illness, he was demoted to grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat; Yue memorialized in his own defense, the ministry recommended dismissal, but favor was shown and he was granted employment as a compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the Ministry of Personnel; in the ninth year he was demoted to grand secretary for failing to detect clerical fraud in which Zhao Yuelian of the Bureau of Transmission had falsely appointed a transport intendant while claiming illness. Yue memorialized in his defense; though dismissal was recommended, the throne showed mercy and allowed him to serve as a compiler.

sentences.zh: 十年，擢鴻臚寺少卿，督山東學政。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was promoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Ceremonial and appointed education commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was made vice director of the Court of Imperial Ceremonial and education commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 累遷大理寺少卿、內閣學士。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review and grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review and grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 母憂歸，服闋，引疾不出。

translations.literal: He returned home on his mother's death; after mourning he pleaded illness and did not take office again.
translations.idiomatic: He went home to mourn his mother, and after the mourning period pleaded illness and declined further office.

sentences.zh: 二十年，卒。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twentieth year.

sentences.zh: 秦瀛，字凌滄，江蘇無錫人，諭德松齡玄孫也。

translations.literal: Qin Ying, styled Lingcang, was a native of Wuxi in Jiangsu and a great-great-grandson of the tutor Songling.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Ying, whose style was Lingcang, came from Wuxi in Jiangsu and was a great-great-grandson of the tutor Songling.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十一年，以舉人召試山東行在，授內閣中書，充軍機章京，洊遷郎中。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year of Qianlong, as a provincial graduate he was summoned for examination at the Shandong traveling palace, appointed secretary of the Grand Secretariat, served as a clerk of the Grand Council, and was repeatedly promoted to director.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year of Qianlong he was summoned for examination at the Shandong traveling palace as a provincial graduate, appointed secretary of the Grand Secretariat, served on the Grand Council staff, and rose to director.

sentences.zh: 五十八年，出為浙江溫處道，有惠政。

translations.literal: In the fifty-eighth year he went out as intendant of Wenzhou and Chuzhou in Zhejiang and governed with benevolent policies.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-eighth year he was posted as intendant of Wenzhou and Chuzhou in Zhejiang, where his benevolent rule won praise.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶五年，擢按察使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jiaqing he was promoted to provincial judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Jiaqing he was promoted to provincial judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 寧、紹、台三府水災，有司匿不報，瀛力言於巡撫，乃得賑。

translations.literal: When Ningbo, Shaoxing, and Taizhou suffered floods, officials concealed the disaster and did not report it; Ying spoke forcefully to the governor and relief was finally granted.
translations.idiomatic: When Ningbo, Shaoxing, and Taizhou were flooded, officials concealed the disaster; Ying pressed the governor until relief was granted.

sentences.zh: 調湖南，衡州歲歉，有司匿不報，方議派濟陝西兵米，瀛复力言於巡撫，留米平糶。

translations.literal: Transferred to Hunan, he found Hengzhou had a lean year which officials again concealed; grain was about to be dispatched to supply Shaanxi troops, but Ying again spoke forcefully to the governor and the grain was kept to sell at fair price.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Hunan, he found Hengzhou suffering famine that officials again concealed while grain was earmarked for Shaanxi troops; Ying again pressed the governor, and the grain was kept for fair-price sale to the people.

sentences.zh: 七年，以病歸。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he returned home on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he retired citing illness.

sentences.zh: 逾兩年，起授廣東按察使，督郡縣治盜，擒著盜梁修平、吳叚喜置諸法。

translations.literal: After more than two years he was recalled and appointed judicial commissioner of Guangdong, supervised the counties in suppressing bandits, and captured the notorious robbers Liang Xiuping and Wu Duanxi and brought them to justice.
translations.idiomatic: After two years he was recalled as judicial commissioner of Guangdong, supervised county efforts against banditry, and captured the notorious robbers Liang Xiuping and Wu Duanxi, who were punished by law.

sentences.zh: 撫瓊州黎匪，嚴禁賭博白鴿票。

translations.literal: He pacified the Li bandits of Qiongzhou and strictly forbade gambling and white pigeon lottery tickets.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified the Li rebels in Qiongzhou and strictly banned gambling and white-pigeon lottery tickets.

sentences.zh: 十年，遷浙江布政使，入覲，乞內用，授光祿寺卿，轉太常寺卿。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred to provincial treasurer of Zhejiang; on presenting himself at court he asked for appointment in the capital, was made director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and then transferred to director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he became provincial treasurer of Zhejiang; at court he asked for a capital post and was made director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, then director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 疏陳廣東治盜事宜，略曰：「海盜始在高、廉，近則闌入廣州。

translations.literal: In a memorial on suppressing bandits in Guangdong he stated in summary: "Pirates first arose in Gaozhou and Lianzhou; recently they have forced their way into Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial on banditry in Guangdong he wrote in summary: "Pirates first plagued Gaozhou and Lianzhou; lately they have pushed into Guangzhou itself.

sentences.zh: 大股如鄭一、烏石二、總兵寶、朱濆等，聲勢甚張。

translations.literal: Large bands such as those of Zheng Yi, Wushi Er, Zongbing Bao, Zhu Fen, and others were very powerful.
translations.idiomatic: Major bands led by Zheng Yi, Wushi Er, Zongbing Bao, Zhu Fen, and others had grown formidable.

sentences.zh: 內地順德、香山、新會三縣，連有肆劫，以馬觀、李英芳為之魁，與海盜勾結，捕急則遁入海中。

translations.literal: In the interior counties of Shunde, Xiangshan, and Xinhui there were repeated robberies led by Ma Guan and Li Yingfang, who colluded with pirates and fled to sea when pursuit grew hot.
translations.idiomatic: Inland in Shunde, Xiangshan, and Xinhui, raids led by Ma Guan and Li Yingfang recurred; they colluded with pirates and fled to sea whenever pursuit intensified.

sentences.zh: 統將出海，藉詞遷延，不能盡力。

translations.literal: Commanding generals put to sea but used excuses to delay and did not exert themselves fully.
translations.idiomatic: Commanding generals put to sea but made excuses to delay and never pressed the fight.

sentences.zh: 黜提督孫全謀，而魏大斌即為之續。

translations.literal: Regional Commander Sun Quanmou was dismissed, but Wei Dabin immediately succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Sun Quanmou was dismissed, only for Wei Dabin to succeed him at once.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為剿捕之法：一曰討軍實。

translations.literal: This subject ventures to think that methods for suppression and capture are: first, to verify military facts.
translations.idiomatic: In my humble view, suppression requires three measures: first, verify the true state of the forces.

sentences.zh: 水師廢弛，則帑餉虛糜。

translations.literal: When the naval forces are neglected, treasury funds are wasted in vain.
translations.idiomatic: When the navy is neglected, treasury funds are squandered to no purpose.

sentences.zh: 洋商、鹽商捐輸寬裕，經手之員尚有侵漁，遣委之將仍復驕惰，非立法痛懲，徒資耗費。

translations.literal: Foreign and salt merchants gave generously, yet the officials in charge still embezzled, and the generals dispatched remained arrogant and idle; without stern laws and punishments, funds are merely consumed.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign and salt merchants gave generously, yet officials in charge still skimmed funds while dispatched generals remained arrogant and idle; without stern laws and punishments, the money is simply wasted.

sentences.zh: 一曰樹聲威。

translations.literal: Second, to establish authority.
translations.idiomatic: Second, establish authority.

sentences.zh: 盜善偵探，非先聲讋人，盜已輕我。

translations.literal: Bandits are skilled at scouting; unless authority is shown first to overawe them, they already despise us.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits scout well; unless we overawe them from the outset, they already hold us in contempt.

sentences.zh: 兵行之日，督撫宜舉觴歡飲；

translations.literal: On the day troops march, the governor and provincial commander should raise cups and drink in celebration;
translations.idiomatic: On the day troops march, the governor and provincial commander should raise cups and feast the men;

sentences.zh: 有功而歸，開轅行賞，不用命者，殺無赦。

translations.literal: when they return with merit, open the yamen gate and grant rewards; those who disobey orders shall be killed without pardon.
translations.idiomatic: when they return victorious, open the yamen gate and reward them; those who disobey orders shall be executed without mercy.

sentences.zh: 一曰戒虛飾。

translations.literal: Third, to guard against empty display.
translations.idiomatic: Third, guard against empty display.

sentences.zh: 擒盜豈能皆真，一念邀功，讞多失實，偶有平反，不復深咎。

translations.literal: Captured bandits cannot all be genuine; with one thought of seeking merit, verdicts often miss the truth, and when cases are occasionally reversed, no deep blame follows.
translations.idiomatic: Not every man seized as a bandit is a real culprit; eager for merit, officials often convict the wrong men, and when cases are reversed, no one is held seriously accountable.

sentences.zh: 嗣後總期弋獲真盜，毋縱毋枉。

translations.literal: Hereafter one should always aim to capture true bandits, neither releasing the guilty nor wronging the innocent.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth the aim must be to catch real bandits — neither letting the guilty go nor wronging the innocent.

sentences.zh: 至守御之法，尤宜急講。

translations.literal: As for methods of defense, these especially should be urgently discussed.
translations.idiomatic: Methods of defense deserve urgent attention above all.

sentences.zh: 砲台防守口岸，口岸多而汛兵少，盜船乘間直入；

translations.literal: Forts defend the ports, but there are many ports and few garrison troops, so pirate vessels slip through at gaps;
translations.idiomatic: Forts guard the ports, but ports are many and garrison troops few, so pirate craft slip through the gaps;

sentences.zh: 巡船复少，不能禦盜，且為盜資。

translations.literal: patrol boats are also few, cannot repel bandits, and even supply them.
translations.idiomatic: patrol boats are too few to repel pirates and even end up supplying them.

sentences.zh: 保甲僅屬虛名，縱役訛索，反成厲政。

translations.literal: The baojia system exists only in name; runners extort under license and it becomes a harsh policy.
translations.idiomatic: The baojia system exists only on paper; runners extort under its name until it becomes an oppressive burden.

sentences.zh: 欲行保甲團練，先須百姓服從。

translations.literal: To carry out baojia and militia training, the people must first be made to obey.
translations.idiomatic: To make baojia and militia training work, the people must first be won to obey.

sentences.zh: 臣以為嚴防守必先澄清吏治，澄吏治必先固民心。

translations.literal: This subject holds that strict defense must first clarify official governance, and to clarify official governance one must first secure the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: In my view, strict defense must begin with clean government, and clean government must begin with winning the people's trust.

sentences.zh: 一曰清獄訟。

translations.literal: First, to clear prison litigation.
translations.idiomatic: First, clear the courts of litigation.

sentences.zh: 粵民好訟，大小案件，諭旨嚴飭，尚多沉擱。

translations.literal: The people of Guangdong love litigation; for cases large and small, though imperial instructions have strictly admonished, many still lie shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong people are litigious; despite repeated imperial orders to expedite cases, many large and small suits still languish.

sentences.zh: 殆由案之初起，遲延不辦，土棍訟師，從而把持，遂至供情屢易，莫可窮究。

translations.literal: This is probably because when cases first arise they are delayed and not handled, local bullies and litigation masters then seize control, so that testimony is repeatedly changed and nothing can be fully investigated.
translations.idiomatic: This is largely because cases are delayed from the outset, local bullies and professional litigators take control, testimony keeps shifting, and the truth can no longer be found.

sentences.zh: 惟有督飭州縣，有一案即清一案，務洗慵惰偏私之習。

translations.literal: Only by supervising and admonishing prefectures and counties to clear each case as it arises can the habits of laziness and partiality be washed away.
translations.idiomatic: Only by pressing prefectures and counties to clear each case as it arises can the habits of laziness and favoritism be rooted out.

sentences.zh: 一曰抑冗濫。

translations.literal: Second, to restrain redundant and excessive staffing.
translations.idiomatic: Second, curb redundant staffing.

sentences.zh: 六計尚廉，近海州縣有緝捕解犯之責，尤宜撙節，庶不虧倉庫而累閭閻。

translations.literal: The Six Assessments value integrity; coastal prefectures and counties bear responsibility for arresting and escorting criminals and should especially practice economy, so that the treasury is not depleted and the people are not burdened.
translations.idiomatic: The Six Assessments prize integrity; coastal counties charged with arresting and escorting criminals must practice economy so the treasury is not drained and the people are not burdened.

sentences.zh: 一令到任，幕友長隨，多人坐食，勢不能復為廉吏。

translations.literal: Once a magistrate takes office, with many secretaries and attendants living off his salary, he can hardly remain an honest official.
translations.idiomatic: Once a magistrate takes office, with secretaries and attendants living off his salary in numbers, he can hardly remain honest.

sentences.zh: 雜職武弁，惟利是圖，稍授以權，即挾製文吏。

translations.literal: Minor civil and military officers seek only profit; give them the slightest authority and they coerce civil officials.
translations.idiomatic: Minor civil and military officers seek only profit; give them the slightest authority and they bully civil officials.

sentences.zh: 雜職差委過多，亦滋擾累。

translations.literal: Too many minor appointments also increase harassment and burdens.
translations.idiomatic: Too many minor appointments only multiply harassment and burdens.

sentences.zh: 一日懲蠹役。

translations.literal: Third, to punish corrupt runners.
translations.idiomatic: Third, punish corrupt runners.

sentences.zh: 胥役熟習地方情形，串同官親家屬，肆為民害。

translations.literal: Runners know local conditions well and collude with officials' kin and household members to harm the people at will.
translations.idiomatic: Runners know local conditions well and collude with officials' kin and household staff to prey on the people.

sentences.zh: 廣東胥役，每有暗通盜匪，收受陋規，此尤不可不嚴行懲創也。

translations.literal: Guangdong runners often secretly communicate with bandits and accept illicit fees; this especially must be sternly punished.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong runners often collude secretly with bandits and take illicit fees; this above all must be sternly punished.

sentences.zh: 三者既舉而吏治澄，吏治澄而民心固，於以舉行保甲團練，無不可使之民，即無不可行之法矣。」

translations.literal: When these three measures are carried out, official governance is clarified; when official governance is clarified the people's hearts are secured, and then baojia and militia training can be implemented — there will be no people who cannot be made to obey, and no methods that cannot be carried out."
translations.idiomatic: Once these three measures are in place, government is clean; once government is clean the people's trust is won, and baojia and militia training can succeed — no people who cannot be rallied, no policy that cannot be enforced."

sentences.zh: 疏上，詔下疆吏採行。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, an edict ordered frontier officials to adopt and carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the throne, an edict ordered frontier officials to adopt its recommendations.

sentences.zh: 遷順天府尹。

translations.literal: He was transferred to governor of Shuntian prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was made governor of Shuntian prefecture.

sentences.zh: 十二年，擢刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was promoted to vice minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was promoted to vice minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 以宗室敏學獄會擬輕縱，議褫職，詔原之，左遷光祿寺卿。

translations.literal: Because in the Minxue case involving a member of the imperial clan the joint recommendation was too lenient, dismissal was proposed; an edict pardoned him and he was demoted to director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: Because the joint recommendation in the Minxue case involving an imperial clansman was too lenient, dismissal was proposed; the throne pardoned him but demoted him to director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 歷左副都御史、倉場侍郎。

translations.literal: He served in succession as vice censor-in-chief on the left and vice minister of the granary yards.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice censor-in-chief on the left and then as vice minister of the granary yards.

sentences.zh: 詔整頓倉場，慮瀛齒衰，以二品頂戴調左副都御史。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the granary yards reorganized; fearing Ying's advanced age, he was transferred to vice censor-in-chief on the left with second-rank insignia.
translations.idiomatic: When the throne ordered the granary yards reorganized, fearing Ying's age he was transferred to vice censor-in-chief on the left with second-rank insignia.

sentences.zh: 尋授兵部侍郎，復調刑部。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed vice minister of war and again transferred to the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made vice minister of war and then returned to the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 瀛治獄平慎，在浙辨定海難民十二人非盜。

translations.literal: Ying handled cases with fairness and caution; in Zhejiang he determined that twelve refugees from Dinghai were not bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Ying judged cases with fairness and care; in Zhejiang he cleared twelve Dinghai refugees wrongly accused as bandits.

sentences.zh: 及海盜誣攀族人，已入告，卒更正省釋。

translations.literal: When pirates falsely implicated his clansmen and charges had already been filed, he finally corrected the case and secured their release.
translations.idiomatic: When pirates falsely implicated his clansmen and charges were already filed, he corrected the record and secured their release.

sentences.zh: 在部治運丁盜米，訐者謂以藥置米中立溢，試之不驗，仁宗親試明其枉，尤為時稱。

translations.literal: In the ministry he tried transport laborers for stealing grain; accusers said medicine had been placed in the grain to make it overflow, but tests did not confirm it; the Renzong Emperor personally tested and proved the accusation false, and this was especially praised at the time.
translations.idiomatic: In the ministry he tried transport laborers accused of stealing grain; accusers claimed medicine had been placed in the grain to make it overflow, but tests failed; Emperor Renzong personally tested the claim and proved it false, winning particular praise.

sentences.zh: 十五年，以病解任。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he resigned his post on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he resigned citing illness.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Daoguang.

sentences.zh: 瀛工文章，與姚鼐相推重，體亦相近雲。

translations.literal: Ying was skilled in literary composition and mutually esteemed with Yao Nai; their styles were also similar.
translations.idiomatic: Ying excelled at prose and held Yao Nai in mutual esteem; their styles were much alike.

sentences.zh: 李宗瀚，字春湖，江西臨川人。

translations.literal: Li Zonghan, styled Chunhu, was a native of Linchuan in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zonghan, whose style was Chunhu, came from Linchuan in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五十八年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifty-eighth year of Qianlong, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the fifty-eighth year of Qianlong, entered the Hanlin Academy, and was made a compiler.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶三年，大考二等，擢左贊善。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiaqing, at the great triennial evaluation he ranked second class and was promoted to left tutor of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: At the triennial evaluation in the third year of Jiaqing he ranked second class and was made left tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 累遷侍講學士，充日講起居注官。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to expositor of the Hanlin Academy and appointed recorder of the emperor's daily lectures and activities.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to expositor of the Hanlin Academy and served as recorder of the emperor's daily lectures and activities.

sentences.zh: 五年，典福建鄉試，母憂歸，服闋，補原官，轉侍讀學士。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he presided over the Fujian provincial examination; he returned home on his mother's death, and after mourning resumed his former post and was transferred to reader of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he presided over the Fujian provincial examination; he mourned his mother, and after the mourning period resumed office and became reader of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 九年，督湖南學政，歷太僕寺卿、宗人府丞、左副都御史。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was education commissioner of Hunan and served in succession as director of the Court of the Imperial Stud, vice director of the Imperial Clan Court, and vice censor-in-chief on the left.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he became education commissioner of Hunan and rose through director of the Court of the Imperial Stud, vice director of the Imperial Clan Court, to vice censor-in-chief on the left.

sentences.zh: 二十年，丁本生母憂，服闋，在籍奏請終生祖母養，允之。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he mourned his birth mother; after mourning he memorialized from his native place to nurse his paternal grandmother for life, and permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he mourned his birth mother; after mourning he memorialized from home to spend his life caring for his paternal grandmother, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 道光三年，遭祖母喪。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daoguang his grandmother died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Daoguang his grandmother died.

sentences.zh: 先是禮臣建議，為父後者為生祖母終三年喪，宗瀚幸奉功令，既而部議仍改期服，宗瀚本生父秉禮已老，而有子四人，以出繼不得終養。

translations.literal: Earlier the Ministry of Rites had proposed that an heir by adoption observe three years' mourning for his birth grandmother; Zonghan was fortunate to follow this decree, but the ministry later still changed it to one year's mourning. Zonghan's birth father Bingli was already old and had four sons; because Zonghan had been given in adoption he could not complete the nursing.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites had earlier ruled that an adopted heir should observe three years' mourning for his birth grandmother, and Zonghan had followed that ruling; but the ministry later reverted to one year. His birth father Bingli was elderly with four sons, and because Zonghan had been given in adoption he could not complete his care.

sentences.zh: 五年，入都，召見，詢家世官資甚悉。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he entered the capital, was summoned to audience, and was questioned in detail about his family's history and official standing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he came to the capital, was received in audience, and questioned in detail about his family and career.

sentences.zh: 宗瀚具陳終養始末，宣宗為之嗟嘆，遂補原官。

translations.literal: Zonghan stated in full how the nursing had begun and ended; Xuanzong sighed at this and restored him to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: Zonghan recounted the whole story of his care for his grandmother; Emperor Xuanzong sighed and restored him to his former post.

sentences.zh: 八年，擢工部侍郎，典浙江鄉試，留學政。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was promoted to vice minister of works, presided over the Zhejiang provincial examination, and remained as education commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was made vice minister of works, presided over the Zhejiang provincial examination, and stayed on as education commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十一年，丁本生父憂，哀毀，扶病奔喪，卒於衢州，以衰服殮，年六十三。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he mourned his birth father; grief destroyed his health, and though ill he hurried to the funeral but died at Quzhou; he was buried in mourning garments at the age of sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year his birth father died; grief shattered his health, and though ill he hurried to the funeral but died at Quzhou, aged sixty-three, and was buried in mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 宗瀚孝謹恬退，中歲以養親居林下十年，書法尤為世重。

translations.literal: Zonghan was filial, cautious, and retiring; in midlife he lived in retirement for ten years to care for his parents, and his calligraphy was especially esteemed in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Zonghan was filial, cautious, and retiring; in midlife he spent ten years in retirement caring for his parents, and his calligraphy was especially prized.

sentences.zh: 韓鼎晉，字樹屏，四川長壽人。

translations.literal: Han Dingjin, styled Shuping, was a native of Changshou in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Han Dingjin, whose style was Shuping, came from Changshou in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 乾隆六十年進士，選庶吉士，授檢討。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the sixtieth year of Qianlong, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the sixtieth year of Qianlong, entered the Hanlin Academy, and was made a reviser.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶九年，改御史。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Jiaqing he was transferred to censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Jiaqing he was made a censor.

sentences.zh: 疏言天主教流傳之害，請申禁以絕根株，從之。

translations.literal: He memorialized on the harm of the spread of Catholicism and asked that the ban be reiterated to uproot it entirely; his request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on the harm of Catholicism's spread and asked that the ban be enforced to uproot it; the throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 以母老請終養，十六年，服闋，補原官。

translations.literal: Because his mother was old he asked to nurse her for life; in the sixteenth year, after mourning, he resumed his former post.
translations.idiomatic: His mother being elderly, he asked to care for her for life; in the sixteenth year, after mourning, he resumed his former post.

sentences.zh: 疏陳四川積弊六事，曰：禁科派以安閭閻，除啯匪以防積漸，查卡房以全民命，禁拐騙以警貪頑，嚴攤捐以養廉潔，覈戎政以歸實效。

translations.literal: He memorialized six long-standing abuses in Sichuan: forbid irregular levies to settle the people; eliminate local ruffians to prevent gradual encroachment; investigate checkpoint houses to protect lives; forbid kidnapping and fraud to warn the greedy and stubborn; strictly limit surcharges to nurture integrity; and verify military administration to restore real results.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized six chronic abuses in Sichuan: ban irregular levies to protect the people; eliminate local ruffians before trouble grows; inspect checkpoint houses to save lives; forbid kidnapping and fraud to warn the corrupt; strictly limit surcharges to nurture honest government; and audit military administration for real results.

sentences.zh: 又言京師賭風大熾，多屬王公大臣輿夫設局，倚勢骫法，帝命指實，下詔嚴治。

translations.literal: He also said gambling in the capital flourished greatly, mostly run by carriage servants of princes and grand ministers who relied on power to bend the law; the emperor ordered specific facts and issued an edict for stern punishment.
translations.idiomatic: He also reported that gambling in the capital flourished, often run by carriage servants of princes and ministers who bent the law by their influence; the emperor ordered specifics and issued an edict for stern punishment.

sentences.zh: 逾日，獲賭案三，大學士、步軍統領祿康輿夫為之魁。

translations.literal: The next day three gambling cases were uncovered, with the carriage servants of Grand Secretary and Metropolitan Infantry Commander Lu Kang as ringleaders.
translations.idiomatic: The next day three gambling rings were broken, with the carriage servants of Grand Secretary and Metropolitan Infantry Commander Lu Kang as ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 親貴近臣，莫不悚息​​。

translations.literal: Imperial kin and close ministers were all struck with fear.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial kin and court favorites were all struck with fear.

sentences.zh: 巡視山東漕務，轉工科給事中、光祿寺少卿，督陝甘學政。

translations.literal: He inspected Shandong grain transport affairs, was transferred to supervising secretary of the Ministry of Works, vice director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and appointed education commissioner of Shaanxi and Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: He inspected Shandong grain transport, became supervising secretary of the Ministry of Works and vice director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and served as education commissioner of Shaanxi and Gansu.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「榆、綏諸州縣倉貯空虛，宜設法籌補，其地資蒙古糧食接濟。

translations.literal: In his memorial he stated: "The granaries of Yulin, Suide, and other prefectures and counties are empty and should be replenished by every means; those regions rely on Mongol grain for relief.
translations.idiomatic: In his memorial he wrote: "Granaries in Yulin, Suide, and neighboring counties stand empty and must be replenished; those regions depend on Mongol grain for relief.

sentences.zh: 今腹裡邊外俱荒，當分別安置撫卹。」

translations.literal: Now both the interior and the frontier are stricken with famine and should be separately settled and relieved."
translations.idiomatic: Now both the interior and the frontier suffer famine and must be relieved by separate measures of settlement and aid."

sentences.zh: 又言：「南山善後事宜，宜行堅壁清野之法。

translations.literal: He also said: "For postwar arrangements in the Southern Mountains, the method of fortified villages and cleared countryside should be applied.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "For postwar recovery in the Southern Mountains, fortified villages and cleared countryside should be enforced.

sentences.zh: 山內流民雜處，最為奸藪，當嚴行保甲，使姦宄無所匿。

translations.literal: Within the mountains displaced people live mixed together and are the greatest nest of villains; baojia should be strictly enforced so that evildoers have nowhere to hide.
translations.idiomatic: Displaced people crowd the mountains and form the greatest nest of villains; baojia must be strictly enforced so evildoers have nowhere to hide.

sentences.zh: 軍中擄脅難民子女，請嚴禁。

translations.literal: In the army refugee men and women and children are seized by force; he asked that this be strictly forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that the army be strictly forbidden to seize refugee women and children by force.

sentences.zh: 南山附近及豫東並經兵燹，宜慎選牧令，以蘇民氣。

translations.literal: Areas near the Southern Mountains and eastern Henan have all suffered from warfare; magistrates should be carefully chosen to revive the people's spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Areas near the Southern Mountains and eastern Henan have all been ravaged by war; magistrates must be carefully chosen to revive the people's morale.

sentences.zh: 川北荒歉，與陝、甘毗連，鹽梟啯匪多出其中，請先事豫防。」

translations.literal: Northern Sichuan suffers famine and borders Shaanxi and Gansu; salt smugglers and local ruffians mostly come from these regions, and he asked for preventive measures in advance."
translations.idiomatic: Northern Sichuan suffers famine and borders Shaanxi and Gansu, whence most salt smugglers and local ruffians come; he asked for preventive measures in advance."

sentences.zh: 並下疆吏如所請行。

translations.literal: All were ordered to frontier officials to carry out as requested.
translations.idiomatic: All were ordered carried out by frontier officials as he had requested.

sentences.zh: 歷鴻臚寺卿、通政司副使、太常寺卿、左副都御史。

translations.literal: He served in succession as director of the Court of Imperial Ceremonial, vice commissioner of the Office of Transmission, director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and vice censor-in-chief on the left.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through director of the Court of Imperial Ceremonial, vice commissioner of the Office of Transmission, director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, to vice censor-in-chief on the left.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，命察視近畿水災，督黃村賑務。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was ordered to inspect flood disasters in the capital region and supervise relief at Huangcun.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he was ordered to inspect floods in the capital region and supervise relief at Huangcun.

sentences.zh: 督福建學政，疏言：「閩中吏治久窳，請不限資格，用廉幹吏補汀、漳、泉三郡望緊要缺，久其任以專責成。

translations.literal: As education commissioner of Fujian he memorialized: "Official governance in Fujian has long been corrupt; qualifications should not be limited, and honest, capable officials should fill the key vacancies in the three prefectures of Tingzhou, Zhangzhou, and Quanzhou, with long tenure to fix responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: As education commissioner of Fujian he wrote: "Government in Fujian has long been corrupt; disregard seniority and appoint honest, capable men to the key posts in Tingzhou, Zhangzhou, and Quanzhou, with long tenure to fix responsibility.

sentences.zh: 漳、泉營伍通盜，請責提鎮立予重典，勿稍袒庇。」

translations.literal: The garrisons of Zhangzhou and Quanzhou collude with bandits; he asked that the provincial commander and regional commander be held responsible to impose severe punishment at once without the slightest favoritism."
translations.idiomatic: The garrisons of Zhangzhou and Quanzhou collude with bandits; he asked that the provincial and regional commanders be held to impose severe punishment without favor."

sentences.zh: 道光六年，遷倉場侍郎，以病罷。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Daoguang he was transferred to vice minister of the granary yards and retired on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Daoguang he became vice minister of the granary yards and retired citing illness.

sentences.zh: 起補工部侍郎，京察，原品休致。

translations.literal: He was recalled to fill the post of vice minister of works; at the capital evaluation he retired at his original rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as vice minister of works; at the capital evaluation he retired at his original rank.

sentences.zh: 卒於家，祀鄉賢祠。

translations.literal: He died at home and was enshrined in the local worthies' temple.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home and was enshrined in the local worthies' temple.

sentences.zh: 朱方增，字虹舫，浙江海鹽人。

translations.literal: Zhu Fangzeng, styled Hongfang, was a native of Haiyan in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Fangzeng, whose style was Hongfang, came from Haiyan in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶六年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the sixth year of Jiaqing, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the sixth year of Jiaqing, entered the Hanlin Academy, and was made a compiler.

sentences.zh: 典雲南鄉試，遷國子監司業。

translations.literal: He presided over the Yunnan provincial examination and was transferred to vice director of studies in the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He presided over the Yunnan provincial examination and became vice director of studies in the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 十八年，教匪之變，方增劾直隸總督溫承惠貽誤地方，黜之。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, during the sectarian rebellion, Fangzeng impeached Governor-General Wen Chenghui of Zhili for harming the region and had him dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, during the sectarian rebellion, Fangzeng impeached Zhili Governor-General Wen Chenghui for mishandling the crisis and secured his dismissal.

sentences.zh: 應詔陳言，論用人理財，略曰：「近今大臣中，罕有以進賢為務者。

translations.literal: In response to an imperial command to state his views, he discussed appointment of men and management of finances, stating in summary: "Among grand ministers today, few make recommending the worthy their task.
translations.idiomatic: In response to an imperial command for his views, he discussed appointments and finances, writing in summary: "Among senior ministers today, few make recommending talent their duty.

sentences.zh: 蓋薦舉之事，易於徇私，黨援交結，不得不防，而大臣亦遂引嫌自避。

translations.literal: For recommendation easily lends itself to favoritism and factional ties must be guarded against, and so grand ministers also avoid the matter out of scruple.
translations.idiomatic: Recommendations easily invite favoritism and factional ties must be guarded against, so ministers avoid the duty out of scruple.

sentences.zh: 夫大臣避徇私之名，而忘以人事君之責，所謂因噎廢食，非公忠體國者所宜有也。

translations.literal: When grand ministers avoid the name of favoritism and forget the duty of serving the ruler through men, this is what is called giving up eating for fear of choking — it is not what those who are loyal and public-spirited toward the state should do.
translations.idiomatic: When ministers shun the charge of favoritism and forget their duty to serve the throne through good appointments, they are throwing away the meal for fear of choking — not the conduct of men who serve the state with public loyalty.

sentences.zh: 至於任用之方，則無過於考言詢事。

translations.literal: As for the method of appointment, nothing surpasses examining words and inquiring into deeds.
translations.idiomatic: As for how to appoint men, nothing surpasses judging their words and inquiring into their deeds.

sentences.zh: 皇上博訪週諮，徐為印證。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should inquire broadly and consult widely, then gradually verify.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should inquire widely and consult broadly, then verify over time.

sentences.zh: 於召對時，各就所長，諭使面陳，果能洞悉原委，又當試之以事，以觀其能踐與否。

translations.literal: At imperial audiences each man should be told to state his strengths face to face; if he truly understands causes from beginning to end, he should then be tested with tasks to see whether he can carry them out.
translations.idiomatic: At imperial audiences each candidate should speak to his strengths in person; if he truly understands his subject, test him with tasks to see whether he can deliver.

sentences.zh: 如或敷奏並無條理，則其人固不足用，而大臣之識見優絀，心地公私，亦可見矣。

translations.literal: If his presentation has no coherence, the man is certainly not fit for use, and the recommending minister's discernment, as well as whether his heart is public or private, can also be seen.
translations.idiomatic: If his presentation lacks coherence, the man is unfit for office, and the recommending minister's judgment and whether his motives are public or private become clear as well.

sentences.zh: 抑臣思臣工居職，苟非闒茸齷齪者流，孰不思自效？

translations.literal: Yet this subject reflects that officials in office, unless they are the incompetent and base sort, who does not wish to serve effectively?
translations.idiomatic: Yet I reflect that officials in office, unless they are incompetent and base, who does not wish to serve effectively?

sentences.zh: 況蒙皇上訓飭至再至三，而猶故習相仍，驟難振拔者，良有數端：條例過繁，文案蒨屑，雖有強敏之吏，而精神疲於具文，其實關於政治民生，轉致不能詳覈。

translations.literal: Moreover, though Your Majesty has admonished again and again, old habits continue and sudden reform is hard — there are truly several reasons: regulations are too numerous and documents too trivial; even capable officials have their energy exhausted by paperwork, and matters that truly concern governance and the people's livelihood cannot be thoroughly examined.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, though Your Majesty has admonished again and again, old habits persist and sudden reform is hard — for several reasons: regulations are too numerous and paperwork too trivial; even capable officials exhaust themselves on documents, and matters that truly concern governance and the people's welfare cannot be thoroughly examined.

sentences.zh: 一也。

translations.literal: This is the first.
translations.idiomatic: This is the first.

sentences.zh: 差務絡繹，公私賠累，身家之卹不遑，民物之懷漸恝。

translations.literal: Commissioned duties come in endless succession, public and private expenses pile up, there is no leisure to care for one's household, and concern for the people gradually grows indifferent.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioned duties come in endless succession, public and private expenses pile up, officials have no leisure for their families, and concern for the people gradually fades.

sentences.zh: 二也。

translations.literal: This is the second.
translations.idiomatic: This is the second.

sentences.zh: 訐告之風，至今益甚。

translations.literal: The fashion of accusation grows worse to this day.
translations.idiomatic: The culture of accusation has grown worse than ever.

sentences.zh: 嘗有以田土、鬥毆細故而叩閽京控者，有司畏其挾制，不得不姑息委蛇。

translations.literal: There have been those who petitioned at the palace gate and brought suits to the capital over trifles of land or brawls; local officials fear their leverage and must indulge them with evasions.
translations.idiomatic: Men have petitioned at the palace gate and brought capital suits over trifling land disputes or brawls; local officials fear their leverage and indulge them with evasions.

sentences.zh: 雖有急公自好者，其尋常蒨屑之事，豈皆一一可達聖聰？

translations.literal: Even those eager for public service and self-restraint — can every trivial matter reach the sacred ear?
translations.idiomatic: Even men eager to serve the public — can every trivial matter reach the emperor's ear?

sentences.zh: 甚至匿名揭帖，無主名之可指。

translations.literal: There are even anonymous placards with no name that can be identified.
translations.idiomatic: There are even anonymous placards with no name to identify.

sentences.zh: 蠹吏猾胥，奸民惡僕，求謀不遂，懲治過嚴，皆可造作飛語，訐及陰私。

translations.literal: Corrupt clerks, crafty runners, wicked commoners, and vicious servants whose schemes fail or who are punished too severely can all fabricate rumors and accuse men's private affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Corrupt clerks, crafty runners, wicked commoners, and vicious servants whose schemes fail or who are punished too harshly can all fabricate rumors and accuse men's private affairs.

sentences.zh: 足使任事之心，不寒而栗，委曲隱忍。

translations.literal: This is enough to make the heart of one who takes on duties shiver without cold and submit in concealed forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: This is enough to make officials who take on real duties shiver with fear and submit in silent forbearance.

sentences.zh: 姦宄橫行，大都由此。

translations.literal: The rampant spread of villainy is mostly due to this.
translations.idiomatic: The rampant spread of villainy stems mostly from this.

sentences.zh: 三也。

translations.literal: This is the third.
translations.idiomatic: This is the third.

sentences.zh: 今皇上欲整飭因循積習，臣愚以為必先除此三者之弊，庶廓然無所疑畏，而得專精實政矣。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty wishes to rectify the accumulated habits of routine indulgence; this subject ventures to think that these three abuses must first be removed, so that officials may be free from doubt and fear and devote themselves to real administration.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty wishes to rectify entrenched habits of routine indulgence; in my humble view these three abuses must be removed first, so officials may act without fear and devote themselves to real governance.

sentences.zh: 經國之方，理財尤要。

translations.literal: In governing the state, managing finances is especially important.
translations.idiomatic: In governing the state, managing finances is especially important.

sentences.zh: 古者以三十年之通制國用，斟酌盈虛，量入為出，用能經常不匱。

translations.literal: In antiquity a thirty-year comprehensive plan governed state expenditure, weighing surplus and deficit and measuring outgo by income, and thus supplies were never exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity a thirty-year budget governed state expenditure, weighing surplus and deficit and measuring spending by revenue, so supplies never ran short.

sentences.zh: 今戶部歲入歲出，年一匯奏。

translations.literal: Today the Ministry of Revenue reports annual income and expenditure once a year in summary.
translations.idiomatic: Today the Ministry of Revenue reports annual income and expenditure once a year in summary.

sentences.zh: 惟中外未合為一，條緒繁賾，極難釐剔。

translations.literal: But central and local accounts are not unified, the threads are numerous and tangled, and sorting them is extremely difficult.
translations.idiomatic: But central and local accounts are not unified, the threads are tangled beyond easy sorting.

sentences.zh: 且凡撥解即謂之出，並未實計所用。

translations.literal: Moreover, every allocation is counted as expenditure without actually calculating what was used.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, every allocation is counted as expenditure without calculating what was actually spent.

sentences.zh: 新舊牽溷，凌雜益甚，而出納諸款，又因有無定之款，盈朒參差。

translations.literal: Old and new accounts are mixed together and confusion grows worse; receipts and disbursements of various kinds further vary in surplus and deficit because of uncertain items.
translations.idiomatic: Old and new accounts are mixed and confusion grows worse; receipts and disbursements further vary because uncertain items throw surplus and deficit out of balance.

sentences.zh: 以故一歲之中，所出幾何，覈之所入，贏餘若干，不能得其實數。

translations.literal: Therefore within a single year how much went out, checked against income, and how much surplus remained — the true figures cannot be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore within a single year how much was spent, checked against income, and what surplus remained — the true figures cannot be known.

sentences.zh: 請旨敕下戶部，歲入歲出，宜合中外為一。

translations.literal: He asked that an imperial order be sent to the Ministry of Revenue to unify central and local annual income and expenditure.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that the Ministry of Revenue be ordered to unify central and local annual income and expenditure.

sentences.zh: 核計贏餘總數，仍取前一二歲所贏餘，確實比較，然後審其輕重緩急，舉一切例內例外諸用款，有可裁省停緩者，酌加撙節。

translations.literal: Calculate the total surplus, still taking the surpluses of the previous one or two years for reliable comparison, then weigh what is urgent and what may wait, and among all regular and exceptional expenditures, wherever cuts or deferrals are possible, practice economy as appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Calculate the total surplus, compare it reliably with the surpluses of the previous one or two years, then weigh what is urgent and what may wait, and cut or defer every regular and exceptional expenditure where economy is possible.

sentences.zh: 庶合於古人通年制用之法，而度支充裕矣。」

translations.literal: Thus one may conform to the ancient method of planning expenditure over the full cycle, and state finances will be ample."
translations.idiomatic: Thus the state may follow the ancient method of planning expenditure over the full cycle, and finances will be ample."

sentences.zh: 二十年，入直懋勤殿，編纂石渠寶笈、秘殿珠林。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he entered regular duty in the Hall of Imperial Study and compiled the Shiqu Baoji and the Midian Zhulin.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he entered regular duty in the Hall of Imperial Study and compiled the Shiqu Baoji and the Midian Zhulin imperial catalogues.

sentences.zh: 尋督廣西學政，累遷翰林院侍讀學士。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed education commissioner of Guangxi and was promoted in succession to reader of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made education commissioner of Guangxi and rose to reader of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 道光四年，大考第一，擢內閣學士。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Daoguang, at the great triennial evaluation he ranked first and was promoted to grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Daoguang he ranked first at the triennial evaluation and was made grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 典山東鄉試。

translations.literal: He presided over the Shandong provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He presided over the Shandong provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 七年，督江蘇學政。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed education commissioner of Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he became education commissioner of Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 十年，卒。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth year.

sentences.zh: 方增熟諳朝章典故，輯國史名臣事蹟，為從政觀法錄，行於世。

translations.literal: Fangzeng was well versed in court regulations and precedents; he compiled the deeds of eminent ministers in the national histories into the Congzheng Guanfa Lu, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Fangzeng was deeply versed in court regulations and precedent; he compiled the deeds of eminent ministers from the dynastic histories into the Congzheng Guanfa Lu, which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 論曰：萬承風、周系英、錢樾以侍從之臣，軺車所至，建白卓然。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Wan Chengfeng, Zhou Xiying, and Qian Yue, as attendant ministers, wherever their inspection carriages went made outstanding proposals.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator writes: As attendant ministers, Wan Chengfeng, Zhou Xiying, and Qian Yue made outstanding proposals wherever their inspection tours took them.

sentences.zh: 秦瀛之治績，李宗瀚之孝行，非僅以文藻稱。

translations.literal: Qin Ying's administrative achievements and Li Zonghan's filial conduct were not praised only for literary ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Ying's record in office and Li Zonghan's filial devotion were honored for more than literary talent alone.

sentences.zh: 韓鼎晉、朱方增侃侃獻納，言有體要，皆風采著於朝列矣。

translations.literal: Han Dingjin and Zhu Fangzeng offered their views frankly and substantively, their words having structure and point, and all showed distinguished bearing in the court ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Han Dingjin and Zhu Fangzeng spoke frankly and to the point in their memorials, and all of them stood out for their bearing at court.
